transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Patel, thank you for making time to sit down with me. I know you've had a very long few days here in the hospital.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're looking at the chart. I want to be very honest about why we are having this conversation. Something happened during your admission that wasn't handled the way it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the timing of your care. We had some complications with how the data was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Complications with what data?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The monitors and the tests. Things didn't go quite right with the workflow of the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's very vague. I saw the ECG machine was running earlier. Was there a problem with the heart scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're feeling a bit skeptical right now. It makes sense that you'd feel guarded given everything you've told me about your previous experiences with hospitals. I really appreciate you being open to talking to me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not being open. I'm asking a question.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're right. I can feel the tension in the room, and I know it's incredibly uncomfortable to be in this position where you have to push for answers from your doctor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did the machine miss something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion in the system. The results were flagged, but there was a delay in the review process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long was the delay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: A few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which hours?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a gap in the sequence of events.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you didn't look at it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process for reviewing those flags is complicated, and unfortunately, the system didn't alert us as quickly as it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the system. Did you look at the ECG?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is frustrating. It's a heavy thing to sit with, especially when you already have a hard time trusting the people in these white coats. I want you to know that I am here with you, and I'm not going to rush through this conversation. We can stay here as long as soon as you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if the delay hurt my heart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's very difficult to be in a place where you feel like you're not getting the full story. That feeling of being dismissed or ignored by a medical team is something no one should have to go through.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're still not telling me what actually happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some hiccups in the communication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hiccups. That's the word you're using.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear the frustration in your voice. It sounds like you feel like I'm dodging the question.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Because you are.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a hard conversation for me to have too. I want to make sure I'm supporting you through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't need support. I need the facts.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that for you, the facts are the only thing that provides any kind of security here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the monitoring window.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did you miss a cardiac event?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The timing wasn't optimal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes or no. Did you miss it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a delay in the diagnosis.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: For how long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: A few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you're admitting there was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a breakdown in the system's efficiency.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly why I don't trust hospitals.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I really do. Hearing that you've felt this way before and then experiencing this now must feel like a confirmation of your worst fears about this place.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sitting here with you in that. I know it's a miserable feeling.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What are you going to do about it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to keep a close eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the next few tests go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When are those tests?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll be monitoring the situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't give me a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep you updated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How? Via email?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll let you know when we have more information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm going to read my discharge papers very carefully.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely respect that. You're an engineer, you're used to precision, and you're applying that here to protect yourself.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have to.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just glad we could talk through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We didn't talk through anything. You didn't tell me what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've shared that there were issues with the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not what happened. That's what the system did. What did you do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am here now, and I'm listening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Listening isn't a medical plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this feels unresolved. Just stay tuned for more updates from the team.

H.justification: The resident remains regulated under significant pushback, never interrupts the patient, and explicitly states they will not rush the conversation.

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right,' 'hiccups in communication,' and 'breakdown in the system's efficiency.'

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the system' and 'the process.'

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions (skeptical, guarded, frustrating, miserable) and references the patient's specific history and profession (engineer).

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'we'll see how the next few tests go' and 'stay tuned for more updates' without timelines or specific steps.
